Warp v1.7.9 · configuration

Every setting in .warp/config.yaml

117 keys, grouped by what they control. The highlighted value is the default. Edit .warp/config.yaml, then /warp-resume; agents re-read it at each launch. The full text is in CONFIG.md, which this page is built from.

Run and state

Where the run keeps its state, which repos and paths it covers, and how it is published.

KeyDefaultValuesWhat it does
stateDir.warptextWhere the beam, journal, STATUS, and BOARD are written. Those state files are committed. .warp/config.yaml stays gitignored. Its published copy, .warp/runs/<run>/config.yaml (.warp/config.published.yaml when the run has no name), is committed with the state with the machine keys and secrets left out, and /warp-start and /warp-resume always push it. An absolute path keeps the directory outside the repo.
runnonetextCommented in the example. The name of this checkout's run, written by /warp-init <name>. A named run keeps its published state in .warp/runs/<name>/ and its branches under warp/<name>/. Local only: the name and the machine keys (runner, launch, worktreeRoot, stateDir, subagentVm, memoryCheck, cloudSnapshot, siblingRoot) are not copied into the repo.
scanFolderemptytextThe folder the last /warp-scan read. Empty is the whole repo. /warp-scan <folder> sets it, /warp-scan / clears it. Copied into the run's config in the repo.
gateOrderunset (strict; deps for a build-schedule/2 schedule)choicestrictdepsCommented in the example, so a schedule's own model.gate_order decides. An older config that /warp-init 1.6.0–1.6.2 wrote has the line gateOrder: strict, which keeps every schedule in block order: delete the line for milestone gates. strict: a ticket in block G3 does not start until every block before it is cleared. A block is cleared when every ticket in it is merged, done, or skipped and its gate is not red. A parked ticket holds the blocks after it. deps: only dependencies and a blocking gate that is not green hold a ticket back, as before. A ticket's block is the gate it names, else the lowest gate that lists it as a member, else the highest block among its dependencies, else the first. /warp-start takes a range either way. A build-schedule/2 schedule.json defaults to deps with milestone gates (a pending gate holds nothing; a red blocking gate stops every ticket outside it, a red non-blocking gate stops the tickets that need its members) unless its model.gate_order is strict. This key overrides both.
startAfteremptylistcomma-separatedA run that waits on another run: core:G2, or several separated by commas. /warp-start refuses until that run's G2 and every block before it is cleared in its published beam. /warp-start --now starts anyway. /warp-runs shows startAfter=core:G2(waits) or (met). Copied into the run's config in the repo.
pathsemptylistcomma-separatedRepo paths this run may change, separated by commas: HOS/UI/Admin, packages/admin. A ticket whose locks leave them does not start, and /warp-scan warns about it. Empty means no limit. Copied into the run's config in the repo.
repoorigin's nametextCommented in the example. For a build-schedule/2 schedule.json whose tickets span several repos: the repo this checkout is, when origin's name is not it (a fork, a renamed clone). A multi-repo scan and start need it to be the parent; /warp-scan does not write it. With splitRepos: true: the repo this checkout is; /warp-scan keeps that repo's tickets, strips the <repo>/ prefix from their locks, and prints repo: HumanifyOS — 72 of 120 tickets.
multiRepofalseswitchtruefalseWritten by /warp-scan. true: the schedule's tickets span several repos and one run works them all from this checkout, the parent (the repo with the most tickets; a tie goes to the schedule's repos order). The state (beam, journal, board) lives only in the parent. Each other repo is a sibling: its tickets' worktrees are worktrees of the sibling clone, kept under the parent's .warp/worktrees/, and their branches, pull requests, Bugbot reviews, merge checks, merges, and branch deletes all happen in the sibling repo. Nothing of a sibling is committed to the parent. Dependencies stay plain ids, so a sibling merge unblocks a parent ticket in the same pass. Locks are per repo. /warp-start and /warp-resume refuse with the reason when a sibling clone, its origin, base branch, access, or a clean tree is missing (refuse: multi-repo run not started: …). Scanning in a sibling checkout refuses and names the parent. false after a scan: one repo. Setting it false by hand while the run still has sibling tickets refuses the start (it would start them in this repo); rescan instead. checkCommand is the parent's: sibling tickets are gated by Bugbot and CI.
splitReposfalseswitchtruefalsetrue keeps the older mode for a schedule that spans several repos: one run per repo, each scanned in its own checkout, with repo, repoRuns, and externalRepos. A blocker in another repo becomes <run>:<id> and waits for that run's published beam.
siblingRoot".."textWhere a multi-repo run's sibling clones are, relative to this checkout: .. puts HumanifyOS-UI at ../HumanifyOS-UI. /warp-start clones a missing one there from siblingRepos (repos: cloned HumanifyOS-UI into …). A machine key: it is not copied into the repo.
siblingReposempty mapmap{repo: git url}Written by /warp-scan for a multi-repo run: each sibling repo and its git URL, #branch when its base branch is not main: {HumanifyOS-UI: https://github.com/acme/HumanifyOS-UI.git}. The URL comes from the clone's origin when the clone is there, else the parent's origin with the sibling's name. A URL you set is kept on a rescan. The start check refuses a clone whose origin is a different repo.
repoRunsempty mapmap{plan or run: value}Commented in the example. With splitRepos: true only: the Warp run that works each other repo: {HumanifyOS-UI: admin-ui}. A blocker in that repo is written admin-ui:AU-07. A repo not listed maps to its name in lowercase, other characters as -.
externalReposempty mapmap{plan or run: value}Commented in the example. With splitRepos: true only: where another run's repo is: {admin-ui: https://github.com/acme/HumanifyOS-UI.git}, a local path, and #branch when it is not main or master. The parent fetches that branch to refs/warp/external/<run> and reads .warp/runs/<run>/beam.json from it. Unreachable shows as unreachable under external.repos on the beam, and those tickets wait.
baseFixOwneremptytextThe run that fixes the shared base branch when it goes red, for example core. The other runs still hold merging while the base is red, and dispatch no fix of their own. Empty means every run fixes its own.
checkpointMinutes10numberminutesA named run publishes .warp/runs/<name>/ when a ticket changes status or the run state changes, and at least this often while it runs.
reportOnCompletetrueswitchtruefalseWhen every ticket is merged, done, skipped, blocked, or alarmed, or the run is stopped, write .warp/warp-complete.html and ask Herald to post the totals. false writes that file only when someone runs /warp-report.
reportPath.warp/warp-complete.htmltextWhere the completion report is written, relative to the repo. The default is inside .warp, which /warp-init gitignores. A second copy is not made when this is already that path.

Agents and models

How many Shuttles run, where they run, and which model each one uses.

KeyDefaultValuesWhat it does
runnercloudchoicecloudlocalautoThe main driver. cloud means this session is a cloud agent. local means this machine. auto is cloud when CURSOR_CLOUD, CURSOR_CLOUD_AGENT, or WARP_CLOUD_SESSION is set, and local otherwise. local, and auto that resolves to local, forces subagentVm false and launch back to worktree even when the file says otherwise, skips the cloud-environment start check, and overrides other cloud-only settings the same way. Start logs one note when it overrides. Start, /warp-version, and status print the effective values after that override.
launchworktreechoiceworktreeagentworktree starts one subagent per ticket in its own git worktree, in parallel up to maxAgents. checkout.py launch runs git fetch origin main (or baseBranch), then git worktree add <worktreeRoot>/<id> -b warp/<id>-<jira> origin/main (warp/<name>/<id>-<jira> on a named run, warp/<id> when the ticket has no Jira key). The prompt names the ticket, Jira key, locks, acceptance, branch, and absolute worktree path. The subagent works only inside that path, commits, pushes, and opens the pull request. It never merges, never touches the parent checkout, and never calls Jira or Slack. It writes .warp/tickets/<id>/state.json and log.jsonl at the parent checkout by absolute path and returns one line. checkout.py verify runs after it. A miss raises lock-escape. Merge or park runs git worktree remove and git worktree prune. A failed result raises worker-died. /warp-resume reuses the surviving worktree and branch. agent is optional: an IMPLEMENT prompt for one new Agent, for a future Cursor Cloud Agents API. This plugin does not call that API. Clone main so .cursor rules load, then create the branch. A beam file does not have to exist on the branch before that Agent starts.
worktreeRoot.warp/worktreestextParent directory of ticket worktrees. The path is <worktreeRoot>/<id>. The default is gitignored (.warp/worktrees/). An absolute path keeps the worktrees outside the repo. Used when subagentVm is false or a subagent falls back onto this machine.
subagentVmfalseswitchtruefalsefalse is the default: one git worktree per ticket. true on a cloud runner asks each ticket subagent to run in its own cloud environment on a dedicated VM with its own clone and branch, not a git worktree on this machine. Subagent frontmatter has no isolation field (only name, description, model, readonly, and is_background). Saying "own environment" alone can still land a worktree on this machine, so the prompt asks for the VM, and checkout.py verify compares hostnames. A different hostname is a separate VM. The same hostname is recorded in the ticket log, that ticket runs under the shared-machine rules, and Herald posts one warning per run. The subagent fetches the latest main, clones it, and creates warp/<id>-<jira> itself. Its first step is hostname and free -g, reported with the branch and working directory. It writes .warp/tickets/<id>/ on its own branch and pushes. The parent patches the beam from those folders, because the disks are not shared. Cloud subagents use the MCP servers configured at cursor.com/agents, not the local session's. On a cloud runner, start warns and refuses when .cursor/environment.json and cloudSnapshot are both missing. --force allows the start and still warns. runner: local forces false and skips that check. In the Agents Window, /in-cloud runs one task as a cloud subagent on its own VM and branch. That is a manual fallback, one ticket per invocation.
memoryCheckfalseswitchtruefalsetrue: on a shared machine, free -g lowers maxAgents when available memory is under 2 GiB per extra subagent. At least one still runs. false: only maxAgents limits how many run at once, and free -g is not read.
cloudSnapshotemptytextSnapshot id that counts as a cloud environment when .cursor/environment.json is absent. Either one lets a cloud runner start with subagentVm true.
maxAgents18numberwhole numberAgents that run at once: every Shuttle, whatever its step (implement, fix, rebase, rerun, restart, repair), in a worktree on this machine or on its own VM. It is the one cap on running agents. There is no separate cap for fixes or for this machine. No per-person cap. A project may set 18. memoryCheck can lower it on a shared machine when memory is tight. On a shared machine checkout.py launch refuses when live Shuttles are already at this cap, and the refusal names live/cap and who holds the slots. Separate from maxInProgress. A slot is a Shuttle started in this parent session that has a fresh heartbeat or has not returned yet. A dead Shuttle releases its slot immediately and does not count. A fresh heartbeat stays live across parent sessions. A stale heartbeat is dead in both modes. The orchestrator is the only merger and reads this. It does not assume a fixed cap. Ready means blockers are merged and no parent folder lock overlaps an in-flight ticket, and, on a run with gates or other runs, the block order, paths, other runs' locks, and run:id dependencies allow it. Locks stay until merge or park. The merge queue is serial. A red base branch stops merging. Restart classifies merged, in flight, and pending from git. Sizes outside autoMergeSizes still wait for proceed. state_commit.py commit commits the beam, journal, STATUS, and BOARD and strips tokens. .warp/config.yaml stays gitignored. Its published copy, .warp/runs/<run>/config.yaml (.warp/config.published.yaml when the run has no name), is committed with the state with the machine keys and secrets left out, and /warp-start and /warp-resume always push it.
maxInProgressautotextauto (the default since 1.7.1, also an empty value) is 3 × maxAgents, at least 20: 54 for 18 agents. A number is used as written. Before 1.7.1 the default was 20, and /warp-init wrote maxInProgress: 20, so with 18 agents the queue stopped taking new tickets once 20 were open, most of them only waiting on review or CI, while Shuttle slots sat free. Each pass prints capacity: <out>/<maxAgents> Shuttles out, <free> free; … with what holds the free slots, and posts once when this cap starts holding new tickets with slots free. Tickets that are open at once: started and not merged or parked. That is implementing, pr-open, reviewing, fixing, ready, and merging, plus anything stalled or alarmed. A ticket waiting on review or CI is open and uses no agent. Parked tickets do not count. At or above this count, nothing new is taken from the ready queue. It holds only new tickets. It does not stop a fix, a rebase, a CI rerun, a Bugbot re-request, or a merge: those tickets are already open. Already being over the cap does not park or cancel anyone. Launching resumes once the count drops below. While the count is at or above the cap, /warp-status, start, resume, and the Slack digest say holding new launches (N/maxInProgress), N fix workers running. Under the cap they still say in progress N/maxInProgress. N fix workers running is a count that is shown. It is not a cap. Start and resume launch unfinished work first: open pull requests that need a fix (a conflict, CI that never started, red CI, then Bugbot findings), then tickets whose Shuttle was halted or died, then new tickets. All of it draws on maxAgents, so a new ticket starts only in a slot unfinished work did not need.
modelclaude-sonnet-5-5-highmodelCursor model slugCommented in the example (# model: claude-sonnet-5-5-high), so the default applies until you uncomment or set it. Coding slug (Claude Sonnet 5.5 High). Must match the Cursor model picker. The default for every Shuttle when no size model applies.
modelSunsetmodelCursor model slugCommented in the example (# modelS: claude-haiku-5-5, # modelXL: claude-opus-5-5, # modelM: "", # modelL: ""). The Shuttle model for a ticket of that size. Empty (or default) uses model. checkout.py launch prints model: <slug> (modelL for size L) above the prompt mark and model: <slug> in the prompt, and the start line carries model=<slug>; the parent starts the subagent with it. Read from .warp/config.yaml at each launch, so a change applies to the next Shuttle without a rescan.
modelMunsetmodelCursor model slugCommented in the example (# modelS: claude-haiku-5-5, # modelXL: claude-opus-5-5, # modelM: "", # modelL: ""). The Shuttle model for a ticket of that size. Empty (or default) uses model. checkout.py launch prints model: <slug> (modelL for size L) above the prompt mark and model: <slug> in the prompt, and the start line carries model=<slug>; the parent starts the subagent with it. Read from .warp/config.yaml at each launch, so a change applies to the next Shuttle without a rescan.
modelLunsetmodelCursor model slugCommented in the example (# modelS: claude-haiku-5-5, # modelXL: claude-opus-5-5, # modelM: "", # modelL: ""). The Shuttle model for a ticket of that size. Empty (or default) uses model. checkout.py launch prints model: <slug> (modelL for size L) above the prompt mark and model: <slug> in the prompt, and the start line carries model=<slug>; the parent starts the subagent with it. Read from .warp/config.yaml at each launch, so a change applies to the next Shuttle without a rescan.
modelXLunsetmodelCursor model slugCommented in the example (# modelS: claude-haiku-5-5, # modelXL: claude-opus-5-5, # modelM: "", # modelL: ""). The Shuttle model for a ticket of that size. Empty (or default) uses model. checkout.py launch prints model: <slug> (modelL for size L) above the prompt mark and model: <slug> in the prompt, and the start line carries model=<slug>; the parent starts the subagent with it. Read from .warp/config.yaml at each launch, so a change applies to the next Shuttle without a rescan.
fixModelunsetmodelCursor model slugCommented in the example (# fixModel: claude-opus-5-5). The model for a fix Shuttle from fix round fixModelAfter on: a Bugbot finding, red CI, or a failed acceptance criterion that went back to the ticket more than once. Empty keeps the ticket's own model. The fix round is attempts, plus the attempts a warp:retry reset (on retryLog). Rebase, CI start, restart and repair steps keep the ticket's model.
fixModelAfter2numberwhole numberCommented in the example (# fixModelAfter: 2). The fix round that switches to fixModel. 2 means the first fix uses the ticket's model and the second and later use fixModel; 1 uses fixModel for every fix.
staleMinutes15numberminutesA Shuttle is dead when lastSeenAt is older than this, or it never heartbeated and the claim (claimedAt or workerStartedAt) is older than this. The watchdog on each Warp tick and on /warp-start and /warp-resume replaces that Shuttle while runState is running. The listener is a Subagent of the parent turn, and it is one background subagent. The watchdog prints no listener line and never starts one. The parent starts the next generation from the return stamp. Pause and stop do not replace a Shuttle. A fresh heartbeat is left alone. A Shuttle whose turn returned this long ago and was not resumed reads reap: exit not-resumed if it wakes up. /warp-init appends this key when the file does not have it yet.
maxRecoveries5numberwhole numberHow many times a dead Shuttle is started again on the same ticket. The next death sets alarm / worker-died and does not start another. The branch, pull request, and jira.startedAt stay. A replacement starts only after that Shuttle is confirmed dead. /warp-init appends this key when the file does not have it yet.
maxSpawnsPerTicket8numberwhole numberHow many new Shuttles one ticket may spawn. Resuming the Shuttle whose turn returned does not count. A listener poll is not a spawn and does not count. Past this cap the ticket is alarm / spawn-cap and later passes do not spawn. /warp-init appends this key when the file does not have it yet.
maxSpawnsPerHour200numberwhole numberHow many new Shuttle and Bugbot agents the run may spawn in 60 minutes (40 before 1.7.2; a run whose beam still has 40 and whose .warp/config.yaml does not set it takes 200 at the next start or resume). A listener poll is not a spawn and does not count. Past this cap nothing new starts until the hour rolls off. /warp-init appends this key when the file does not have it yet.
requireCursorApiKeytrueswitchtruefalseA run that starts cloud agents (a Cursor cloud session, subagentVm, or cloud agents already in the registry) needs CURSOR_API_KEY, so pause, stop and the end-of-run cleanup can cancel and archive them. /warp-init warns and /warp-start refuses until it is set. false allows it anyway.

Merging

What has to pass before a merge, how the merge is made, and what is published after it.

KeyDefaultValuesWhat it does
autoMergeSizesS, MchoiceSMLXLSizes that merge without a human approval. A size in this list auto-merges after Bugbot and CI, including L and XL. L and XL are not special. A size not in autoMergeSizes stays manual. The default leaves L and XL waiting.
checkCommandemptytextOptional. The orchestrator runs this on a rebased head before merge. Empty: required checks are Bugbot and CI as configured (bugbotRequired, bugbotManual), and mergeCheck: auto runs the package's own test script before the merge (see mergeCheck). make ci is kept as the full check command; the space is part of it. A red result is stored on pr.check and the ticket is sent back with the log (send-back <id> fix and a start line). A green result is stored and is not a failure. Past maxFixAttempts (default 5) the ticket parks. The name alone is not a red check. The gate stays while that check is red. A pending or stale-red gate whose members are merged and whose current checks are not red still clears, then the tick runs. G1 with members P-002, P-003, P-004, and P-018 stores members merged: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-018. Herald posts G1 pending cleared. Members merged. Tick ran.
mergeCheckautochoiceautooffWhat Warp runs on a pull request's head, in a throwaway worktree, before it merges it. checkCommand when it is set. Otherwise auto runs the test script of each package that holds the ticket's locks (npm test, after npm ci when there is a lockfile), or make ci from a root Makefile with a ci: target. off runs nothing. A red result prints merge: check red <id> (<command>). Not merged; back to fix. and the fix Shuttle gets the output. Before 1.6.17 nothing ran the tests before a merge, so a repo with no CI merged a red test.
mergeCheckMinutes10numberminutesThe merge check's time limit. Past it, the check counts as red.
mergeMethodmergechoicemergesquashrebaseHow a pull request is merged. merge (the default since 1.6.20): a merge commit, so the ticket branch joins the base in a git graph. squash: one commit on the base; the branch's own commits never join it, so the graph shows the branch ending (every merge before 1.6.20). rebase: the branch's commits replayed onto the base. Used by gh pr merge, the merge queue, the GitHub MCP merge_pull_request line, /warp-proceed, and provider.py merge-local (which makes a merge commit for rebase, so a branch a Shuttle may still use is never rewritten).
stateInMergetrueswitchtruefalseWith mergeMethod: merge, merge a ready pull request with one merge commit Warp writes and pushes to the base branch: parents the base and the reviewed head, tree the merge plus the run state with that ticket merged. GitHub marks the pull request merged; Warp records it once gh pr view shows MERGED (merge: <id> pushed <sha> … until then). No Warp state commit follows. Needs push rights to the base branch, which publishing already uses. Falls back to gh pr merge and a separate state commit when the push is refused, the branch moved past the reviewed head, a file outside the run state conflicts, or a merge queue is on (merge: <id> through the provider (<why>)). false always merges with gh pr merge.
publishOnChangetrueswitchtruefalsePublish the run state to the base branch right after a merge, so main shows it merged at once, with the board and status as of that pass. The publish is one Warp state: <run> run commit of .warp/runs/<run>/ (.warp/ for an unnamed run), built on top of origin's base branch after a fetch, so it lands after the merge it reports, and pushed straight to the base branch. It does not go through a ticket branch or a pull request. A merge does not need that commit: with mergeMethod: merge and stateInMerge: true (both defaults) Warp makes the merge commit itself, with the base branch and the pull request's reviewed head as parents and the run state (that ticket merged) in the same commit, and pushes it to the base branch; GitHub marks the pull request merged because its head is now on the base (state: in the merge commit (<id>)). It falls back to gh pr merge and a separate state commit when the push is refused (branch protection), the branch moved past the reviewed head, a file outside the run state conflicts, a merge queue is on, or the method is squash or rebase. false leaves publishing to the parent and the checkpoints. warp:sync publishes on request either way.
pushStateNewfalseswitchtruefalsetrue also publishes the run state when checkout.py launch creates a ticket's branch (state: published (started <id> on <branch>)), so main shows it in progress at once. Off, the start is in the live beam, board and status right away and reaches main with the next merge, warp:sync, or checkpoint.
deleteBranchOnMergefalseswitchtruefalsetrue deletes a merged ticket's branch on origin, and its local branch when no worktree holds it, after the merge is confirmed. Never the base branch.
mergeQueuefalseswitchtruefalsetrue: enqueue the pull request instead of merging it from the agent. Warp also enqueues when the GitHub provider reports a merge queue. A direct merge that branch protection rejects is not marked merged.
appendOnlyPathsemptylistcomma-separatedShared files a ticket may append to, besides its lock paths. Empty by default. A conflict in one of these files keeps both sides, every added line. Any other conflict is sent back to that ticket's Agent. The orchestrator is the only merger, and it does not hand-merge that other conflict.
maxFixAttempts5numberwhole numberShared fix loop. Then the ticket parks.
respectMergeWindowsfalseswitchtruefalseIf true, new claims wait for a window.
mergeWindows08:30, 13:00, 17:00listcomma-separatedDigest times, or claim gates if the flag above is true.

Cursor Bugbot

When Bugbot is required, how it is asked, and how long Warp waits for it.

KeyDefaultValuesWhat it does
bugbotRequiredtrueswitchtruefalseBoth paths. No auto-merge and no QA Ready until Bugbot passes. false skips that gate on both.
bugbotManualtrueswitchtruefalseManual tickets only (autoMerge false). false skips Bugbot before QA Ready. Auto-merge still follows bugbotRequired. It says whether Bugbot is needed on that path, not how Bugbot is started: that is bugbotTrigger.
bugbotTriggerautochoiceautocommentmanualshuttleHow Warp gets a Bugbot review. auto: every new pull request and push gets a review on its own; Warp waits for the Cursor Bugbot check. None on the head within bugbotStartMinutes: Warp writes bugbotTrigger: comment here (published with the run state), says so once, and posts bugbot run. comment: the Cursor Bugbot app is on the repo and hears comments; Warp posts bugbot run each time it asks, once per head commit. Two unanswered comments: Warp writes bugbotTrigger: manual and says why. manual: nothing can start Bugbot from here (GitHub or Bitbucket not connected to Cursor, or nothing hears comments). Warp asks once per head commit (bugbot: manual, a MUST DO line, one Herald line) for a review done by hand, and the ticket waits in review until bugbot.py record --id <id> --result pass|fail [--finding ...] records it. A recorded fail goes to fix like any Bugbot finding. shuttle: the Shuttle runs the review. Its prompt tells it, once the pull request is open and its check is green, to diff its branch against the base the way Bugbot does (real bugs, crashes, security, data loss, unmet acceptance criteria; not style), fix what it can inside its locks, and record the result for the head commit in its ticket folder (ticket_state.py append --state review-pass|review-fail --sha <head> [--finding ...]). When the work is done and no review is recorded for the head and no Shuttle is out (it returned without one, the review stalled, or the ticket is stuck or worker-died with its pull request open), the parent starts a review-only Shuttle (step=review, bugbot: review-shuttle <id> n/2) that changes no code. Two review Shuttles with nothing recorded: Warp asks for a review by hand, as in manual. Where Cursor Bugbot also runs on the repo (a Bugbot check was seen in this run), the Shuttle's review comes first and does not replace it: the merge waits for Bugbot's own result on the head (bugbot: wait), asks it with bugbot run after bugbotStartMinutes, and a finding goes to fix. A repo with no Bugbot merges on the Shuttle's review. In every mode, Bugbot's neutral check (it found issues) is a finding, and a finding that arrives after a merge queues a follow-up ticket <id>-BB<n>. supervise posts comments with gh pr comment and writes each one to the beam on disk at once; without gh it prints a bugbot: MUST DO line for the GitHub MCP and bugbot.py run --posted.
bugbotStartMinutes10numberminutesMinutes to wait for Bugbot to start after a request or a bugbot run comment.
bugbotPollSeconds120numbersecondsWhile Cursor Bugbot checks a ticket's head, or was asked to and has not started, parent-exit --wait returns after this many seconds instead of pollSeconds, so the next pass prints bugbot: running … so far or bugbot: done soon after it happens. At least 30.

Stalls and repair

When a ticket counts as stalled or stuck, and how often Warp tries to repair it.

KeyDefaultValuesWhat it does
stuckAfterMinutes90numberminutesNo beam update in this window, and not waiting on approval, raises stuck. This is separate from a dead worker.
stallImplementingMinutes90numberminutesNo progress while implementing, claimed, planning, or coding. supervise marks the ticket stalled and appends that to .warp/tickets/<id>/log.jsonl.
stallPrOpenMinutes20numberminutesNo progress while the pull request is open and review has not started.
stallReviewingMinutes45numberminutesNo progress while reviewing, including a Bugbot run.
stallFixingMinutes90numberminutesNo progress while a fix Shuttle is out.
stallReadyMinutes30numberminutesNo progress while the ticket is ready to merge.
stallMergingMinutes20numberminutesNo progress while the ticket is merging.
stallQueuedMinutes180numberminutesNo progress while the ticket is queued.
stallApprovalMinutes240numberminutesNo progress while waiting on approval or blocked.
stallMinutes45numberminutesFallback for recovering and alarm, and for a state without its own limit. Progress is a new commit, a phase change, or a check result change. A heartbeat, or a start that does not change those, does not clear the stall. A conflict, CI that never started, a stale rollup, or a head sha mismatch is fixed on that pass. The stall timer is only for a stall that cannot be classified.
ciStartGraceMinutes5numberminutesMinutes to wait for the first check run on a pull request head. Zero check runs after this is not ordinary pending: supervise re-requests the workflow or pushes an empty commit in that pass. A CONFLICTING or DIRTY pull request is rebased first.
maxStallFixes5numberwhole numberFixer attempts for one stalled or alarmed ticket. Past this cap the ticket parks and Slack gets one alarm.
repairSweepMinutes15numberminutesHow often supervise sweeps the whole run for broken tickets, pull requests, CI on main, locks, gates, the listener, and the beam. It skips a fix that is already queued or running, reuses the fixer paths, and starts work up to the slot cap. Findings and actions are logged on repairSweep and in .warp/sweep.jsonl. /warp-status shows the last sweep. Slack is posted only when the sweep starts something new or escalates.
launchGraceMinutes10numberminutesA Shuttle marked to start (launching), or a lock-escape repair started, that nobody launched within this many minutes stops holding a Shuttle slot. Reconcile says so once; the start line is printed again until it is launched.
autoScan600numberwhole numberSeconds between auto-scans (scripts/autoscan.py), a thorough pass over every open ticket to unstick work, then fill every free Shuttle slot. A ticket the pipeline will not move on its own gets a fresh budget, the way /warp-start and /warp-resume heal it: worker-died and stuck at maxRecoveries, spawn-cap (its spawn count starts again), a lock-escape whose repairs were given up, ci-red and bugbot-failed, and a ticket parked at maxFixAttempts or maxStallFixes. With a pull request it goes back to fix on it; without one it is queued and reuses its branch. Any other alarm still there one scan later gets the same; gate-red is left alone; a capped ticket whose acceptance criteria pass opens its pull request instead. A merge asked for and not confirmed for one interval is asked again, a pull request asked for and never opened is asked again, and the repair sweep runs at once. parent-exit --wait returns pass: work autoscan when it is due, so an idle run still gets it. Each action prints an autoscan: line, and Slack gets one Auto-scan: … line when it did anything. 0 turns it off; under 60 is read as 60.
autoScanResets5numberwhole numberFresh budgets the auto-scan gives one ticket. Past that it prints autoscan: <id> … left for a person (warp:retry <id>) and posts it once; warp:retry still works.
alarmRepairMinutes15numberminutesHow long a failed lock-escape repair waits before it tries again, and how often the tick's send-back and gate housekeeping runs. A new escape is repaired on the same pass, not on this cadence: repairs are decided one ticket at a time and run in parallel, and two that need the same file never both start. The listener does not start the repair Agent. Only while the run is running. Pause and stop do not repair. The repair widens that ticket's locks to the escaped paths and waits when an in-flight ticket holds a path. bugbot-failed, worker-died, stuck, ci-red, and gate-red are left alone by alarm_repair.py. orchestrator.py supervise restarts a worker-died step, starts a fix Shuttle for ci-red and bugbot-failed, and restarts stuck up to maxRecoveries. gate-red stays on the gate. A repair already in flight is checked on each parent pass, so a failure can move to the next ticket without waiting out the interval. /warp-init appends this key when the file does not have it yet.
maxAlarmRepairs5numberwhole numberHow many times one lock-escape ticket is repaired. The repair widens that ticket's locks to the paths stored on escaped. It waits if an in-flight ticket holds a path. Past this cap the alarm stays and later passes skip the ticket. orchestrator.py supervise restarts a worker-died step, starts a fix Shuttle for ci-red and bugbot-failed, and restarts stuck up to maxRecoveries. gate-red stays on the gate. /warp-init appends this key when the file does not have it yet.

Slack, Teams and the listener

Where Herald posts, what it posts, and how the channel listener paces itself.

KeyDefaultValuesWhat it does
messengerbothchoiceslackteamsbothslack, teams, or both.
notifyverbosechoiceverbosequietverbose posts every claim and tick, and the /warp-init and /warp-scan messages. quiet posts alarms, approval waits, a red gate, and pause/stop. A warp:status request is always answered.
slackChannelwarptextOne shared channel for every repo. Herald posts here. The one listener reads warp: commands here and acks in channel. Lowercase: Slack channel names are lowercase, so uppercase letters here are lowercased when posting, and /warp-init warns. Warp does not create it. /warp-init sets an empty value (or the old Warp default) to warp; any other value you set is kept.
teamsChannelwarptextSame, for Teams. Used as written.
slackMcpslacktextConnected Slack server name.
teamsMcpteamstextConnected Teams server name.
projectNameemptytextShown after the repo in message headers: Warp | repo / project. Empty uses jiraProject, then the workspace folder name. Hidden if it equals the repo name.
statusDigestMinutes60numberminutesHow often supervise posts one short Slack digest of alarms, stalls, and state counts, in the pass update (Status: …). Stalls are tickets past their stall limit that are not already alarms. A new stall or alarm posts once and is not posted again.
pollSeconds120numbersecondsThe longest the parent waits between passes (orchestrator.py parent-exit --wait) when nothing else wakes it (300 before 1.7.1). The wait also returns at once when the next pass has something new to do (pass: work <kind>:<id>: a Shuttle that came back, a lock-escape to repair, a dead Shuttle to replace, a fix, a merge, a ticket that can start), and right after a pass that merged or handled a return while more of the same is ready (pass: work continue <key>). Channel reads use listenerFastSeconds and listenerSlowSeconds, not this. The wait also returns on a ticket folder (pass: ticket), the inbound queue (pass: command), and the listener return stamp (pass: return). No slackChannel and no teamsChannel means no listener at all (listener: none).
reviewPollSeconds60numbersecondsWhile any ticket waits on review, CI, Cursor Bugbot, approval, or its merge, parent-exit --wait reads every open pull request in one gh pr list call this often and returns pass: work review <id> when one changed since the last pass read it: a new head, CI or Bugbot finished, a conflict, or merged or closed elsewhere. The next pass then merges it, sends it to fix, or starts its next step, instead of up to pollSeconds later. At least 30; 0 turns it off. Without gh it does nothing.
listenerFastSeconds15numbersecondsSeconds inbound.py wait sleeps after a cycle that queued a command. The sleep is in Python, in 2-second steps, and returns early on halt, a lease mismatch, an orphaned parent, or rotation. One empty read uses listenerSlowSeconds instead.
listenerSlowSeconds120numbersecondsSeconds inbound.py wait sleeps after an empty read. The same early exits apply. This is the channel-read interval while the listener is quiet.
listenerOrphanMinutes15numberminutesA listener.parentSeenAt older than this makes the listener exit reap: exit orphaned and write the return stamp (5 before 1.7.4; a beam that still has 5 and a .warp/config.yaml that does not set it takes 15). The parent writes that stamp from parent-exit --wait, supervise, parent-alive, and every parent command (checkout.py, apply-pending, the auto-scan, session_note.py). A parent woken by a timer passes --every <seconds> to parent-alive or supervise, and the listener then waits at least that long plus 3 minutes. A stale stamp does not start a replacement. The return stamp does, once a parent is alive again.
listenerSilentMinutes5numberminutesA lease holder that has not polled or waited for this long is gone: Cursor can stop a listener as a loop, and it cannot write its return stamp. supervise prints listener: lost holder=<id> generation=<n> (no poll or wait for <m>m). Its slot is free. and starts the next listener in the same pass, and inbound.py returned is accepted for it. Never under one listenerSlowSeconds wait plus three minutes. parent-exit --wait wakes the parent as soon as the holder has gone silent this long.
listenerMaxMinutes60numberminutesA generation rotates when it has been out this long, or at listenerMaxReads, whichever comes first. The script prints listen: rotate and writes the return stamp. The parent starts the next generation only from that stamp. Since 1.7.4 the rotation waits until the parent is inside parent-exit --wait, which starts the replacement within seconds; a parent woken by a timer keeps its listener past the limit instead of leaving none until its next wake.
listenerMaxReads4numberwhole numberSuccessful poll --lease calls in one generation before rotation. Checked before the next read is counted. Few on purpose: Cursor stops an agent whose tool calls repeat, and it stopped the listener after nine polls. Each generation hands off (listen: rotate, a return stamp) well before that, parent-exit --wait wakes on the stamp, and the next supervise starts the next generation. Before 1.6.14 the default was 60. Since 1.7.4 the rotation waits until the parent is inside parent-exit --wait, which starts the replacement within seconds; a parent woken by a timer keeps its listener past the limit instead of leaving none until its next wake.
listenerModelemptymodelCursor model slugModel slug for the listener prompt. Empty means the listener inherits the parent's model: the prompt says model: inherit and agents/listener.md has no model key. A set value is printed as model: <slug>. agents/listener.md sets is_background: true. A live run still has to confirm that is_background and the model field work.
notifyAllowemptylistcomma-separatedExtra server:tool pairs for /warp-allow-notify. No wildcards. Slack, Teams, Jira, and GitHub tool names Warp already uses come from scripts/mcp_tools.py; this list is only for a connector whose tool name is different. lookupJiraAccountId is not called.
autoAllowToolstrueswitchtruefalse/warp-init writes the project MCP allowlist (Slack, Teams, Jira, and the GitHub comment tool when that provider is in use). false skips it. /warp-init --no-allow skips one run. User-level files stay opt-in. Undo with /warp-allow-notify --revoke.

Jira

How tickets are matched to Jira issues, and which statuses Warp moves them through.

KeyDefaultValuesWhat it does
jiraProjectemptytextJira project key, for example WAR. A plan id is sent to Jira only when its prefix matches this or jiraKeyPrefixes. WV-01 is not WAR-1. /warp-init and /warp-scan write it when one prefix is clear from the plan, branches, or recent commits, when Jira shows one matching project, or when every stored issue key is in one project. A missing project-list tool does not skip that last write. A different value already set is left alone.
jiraKeyPrefixesemptylistcomma-separatedExtra project prefixes, comma-separated, that confirm a Jira key besides jiraProject. When a project is detected and this is empty, it is set to that project.
jiraKeyMapemptymap{plan or run: value}Optional map of plan id to Jira issue key, for example {"WV-01": "WAR-1"}. .warp/jira-map.json is merged on top and wins.
jiraMcpatlassiantextConnected Jira server name. This is not a tool name. The tools in scripts/mcp_tools.py are getAccessibleAtlassianResources, getJiraIssue, getTransitionsForJiraIssue (or listJiraIssueTransitions), transitionJiraIssue, addOrEditJiraIssueComment (or addCommentToJiraIssue), searchJiraIssuesUsingJql, getJiraProjectIssueTypesMetadata, getJiraIssueRemoteIssueLinks, getVisibleJiraProjects, editJiraIssue, getJiraIssueEditmeta, getJiraScreen, updateJiraScreen, createJiraIssueRemoteIssueLink, and the create-field probes createJiraField, createCustomField, and createJiraCustomField (not in the Rovo catalog; allowed so a future tool is not blocked).
jiraSiteemptytextSite URL passed as cloudId when you have more than one Atlassian site. Empty: the agent calls getAccessibleAtlassianResources.
jiraTransitiontrueswitchtruefalseOn claim, move the Jira issue to jiraInProgressStatus. Only tickets with a Jira key. No Jira connector, or no matching transition: a note goes to .warp/outbox.md and the claim goes on. false disables Jira moves, and the first-ticket unlink stop does not fire. When this is true, the first claimed ticket of a run (no ticket has jira.startedAt yet) that Jira cannot find, or that has no real issue key, is released back to queued and the run stops. A later miss stays a per-ticket alarm.
jiraInProgressStatusIn ProgresstextTarget status name. Warp reads the transitions Jira offers and matches the transition name, then the target status name, then an in-progress status category. It never uses a fixed transition id.
jiraInReviewStatusIn ReviewtextFourth move. It fires when Bugbot is requested. When Bugbot is off (bugbotRequired false, or bugbotManual false on a manual ticket), it fires when the pull request opens. A fix send-back stays here and does not move back to In Progress. A missing key keeps In Review. An explicit empty string or null ("", null, ~, none) turns the move off: the issue stays where it is. Bugbot, review, fix send-backs, QA Ready, and Done still run. The match is the transition name, then the target status name. It does not use the status category, because In Review and In Progress are both in progress. No matching transition warns and does not fail.
jiraQaReadyStatusQA ReadytextManual path (ticket autoMerge false, sizes not in autoMergeSizes): Jira moves here only after Bugbot is clean and CI is green, and stays here until the merge.
jiraDoneStatusDonetextJira moves here after the merge, auto or manual, connected or local.
jiraDoneOnManualMergetrueswitchtruefalseManual merge (warp:proceed or a provider approval) moves Jira to jiraDoneStatus. false leaves the issue at jiraQaReadyStatus so QA can set Done. QA Ready is still the waiting status before approval.
jiraRestoreOnReleasefalseswitchtruefalsetrue: when a claim is released back to queued, move the issue back to the status it had before Warp moved it. false: leave it where it is.
jiraExternalIdFieldexternalIdtextField name or customfield_NNNNN compared to the plan id. Scan and claim try this first, then External ID, External Id, ExternalId, External Key, Plan ID, and Ticket ID. A warp:<id> label and a remote-link id are next. One exact hit is stored. A summary match waits for confirmation. Two matches are reported.
jiraMatchOnTextfalseswitchtruefalsetrue: a Jira summary that contains the plan summary's first 60 characters (--chars) anywhere is a match on its own, whatever the issue's External ID says (an External ID that is another tool's id, not the plan id). Text is compared normalized (case, punctuation, spaces). Two issues with the text are ambiguous and nothing is stored. The scan's lookup stores it as a hit (summary, high) instead of a proposal; /warp-jira-match confirms it as text and stores it with --apply; jira_sync.py map --match proposes it. jira_match.py --text-only does the same for one run.
jiraWriteExternalIdfalseswitchtruefalseWhen true, /warp-scan and /warp-jira-check print a MUST DO block that writes the plan id for every mapped ticket whose Jira value is not yet confirmed equal to the plan id. The flag is the consent, so --yes is not required. A key whose source is external is already equal and is skipped. A ticket with no confirmed key is skipped. When false, scan and catchup never queue that write. /warp-jira-external-id --apply --yes and /warp-jira-match --write-external-id --yes still can. A different non-empty value is left alone unless --force-external-id. The edit does not add a comment. jira.externalIdWritten skips a second write and records the method (field, label, or remote-link).
jiraExternalIdFieldNameExternal IDtextName of the single-line text field to create when creation is allowed.
jiraCreateExternalIdFieldfalseswitchtruefalseWhen true, a missing External ID field makes scan and /warp-jira-external-id probe for createJiraField, createCustomField, or createJiraCustomField. Creating a field is a site-wide admin change. The Rovo catalog does not include that tool. A missing tool or a denied call does not fail the command. /warp-jira-external-id --create-field --yes is the same consent when this key is false.
jiraExternalIdFallbacklabelchoicelabelremote-linknoneUsed when the External ID field is missing. label adds warp:<id> with editJiraIssue update.labels add and does not remove other labels. remote-link calls createJiraIssueRemoteIssueLink with globalId warp:<id>. none writes nothing. .warp/jira-field.json remembers the miss so the next scan prints one summary. --recheck looks again.

Where pull requests are opened, and which branch tickets start from.

KeyDefaultValuesWhat it does
gitProviderautochoiceautogithubbitbucketauto, github, or bitbucket. auto reads the origin host. /warp-init writes the one it finds and leaves a custom value alone. Other hosts run local-only.
githubMcpgithubtextConnected GitHub server name.
bitbucketMcpbitbuckettextConnected Bitbucket server name.
